<p>I am a PhD candidate at the University of Toronto's [Faculty of Information](https://ischool.utoronto.ca/student-profile/inessa-de-angelis/), where I use computational and statistical methods to study how technology is changing political communication and the relationship between political actors and the public. </p>

<p> My Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC)-funded doctoral research examines online harassment faced by Canadian politicians as one dimension of these changing political relationships, investigating its forms, impacts, and gendered dimensions. I bring more than a decade of experience working in federal Canadian politics to this research, alongside previous experience as a Researcher at the [Pol Comm Tech Lab](https://www.polcommtech.com/) at the University of Ottawa.</p> 

<p> My research has been published in journals such as *Social Media + Society*, the *Canadian Journal of Political Science*, and *Computational Communication Research*. My work and commentary have also been featured in media outlets including *The Guardian*, *Canada's National Observer*, *The Conversation*, and *The Hamilton Spectator*.</p>

<p> I hold a Master of Information from the University of Toronto and an Honours Bachelor of Arts with a Double Major in Communication and History from the University of Ottawa.</p>

::: {style="text-align: left;"}
